eyebrow: Turning the last two lessons into habits

steps.label: GRANT TO ROLES, NOT USERS
steps.sub: privileges to roles, roles to users — never the other way around

steps.label: LEAST PRIVILEGE
steps.sub: grant only what's needed now; add more later rather than over-granting

steps.label: GUARD ACCOUNTADMIN
steps.sub: keep membership to a tiny handful of people

steps.label: SEPARATE DUTIES
steps.sub: USERADMIN creates roles, SECURITYADMIN grants them — don't collapse this into ACCOUNTADMIN

steps.label: AUDIT REGULARLY
steps.sub: SHOW GRANTS isn't a one-time setup step

eyebrow: Future grants — don't let new objects slip through
code:
GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN SCHEMA governance_demo.sales TO ROLE analyst_role;
GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE VIEWS IN SCHEMA governance_demo.sales TO ROLE analyst_role;
caption: Future grants apply automatically to objects that don't exist yet — so a new table isn't quietly forgotten and left inaccessible, or worse, over-privileged by habit.

eyebrow: Auditing what a role can actually do
code:
SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE analyst_role;
SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE governance_demo.sales.orders;
caption: Two directions worth checking: what a role has (GRANTS TO), and who has access to an object (GRANTS ON).

subtitle: Chapter 2 begins: a role can have access to a table and still not see the raw values in it.
